title: "Research Products: Manuscripts, Abstracts, Posters, Dashboards, and Briefs"

{#sec-research-products}

Success at RIPLRT is broader than grants and papers. We define it to include **student development, presentations, skills, reproducible tools, and reputation** alongside traditional outputs. This chapter catalogs the products we make and how we make them well.

## Our product portfolio

| Product | Primary audience | Owned by (typical) | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peer-reviewed manuscript | Scientific community | Writing Lead + Analysis Lead | `manuscript-planning-sheet.qmd` |
| Conference abstract | Scientific community | Project Lead / mentee | `conference-abstract-planning.qmd` |
| Poster | Conference attendees | Mentee (often first product) | (see abstract sheet + assets) |
| Reproducible notebook | Internal + open science | Reproducibility / Analysis Lead | `reproducible-analysis-checklist.qmd` |
| Clinician-facing dashboard | Clinicians, agencies | Visualization/Dashboard Lead | (pod charter) |
| Community risk brief | Communities, partners | Science Communication Lead | (pod charter) |
| Public-health playbook | Agencies, decision-makers | Project Lead + SciComm Lead | (pod charter) |
| Bilingual sci-comm content | General public | Science Communication Lead | (pod charter) |

## Manuscripts

- Start with the **Manuscript Planning Sheet**: target journal, key message, figures, authorship plan, and timeline — *before* drafting.
- One **Writing Lead** coordinates drafting and submission; sections are delegated to build skills (figure lead, methods lead, literature-synthesis lead).
- Every number and figure traces back to a **reproducible notebook** (@sec-reproducible).
- Aim for the IAP cadence: a steady, thematically coherent manuscript pipeline organized around our four themes — aeroallergen/fungal early-warning science; respiratory severity and care pathways; biomarker/microbiome signatures; and equity-stratified environmental risk.

## Abstracts and posters

- Abstracts are often a **mentee's first scholarly product** — treat them as real training, not filler.
- Maintain a shared **abstract calendar** of society deadlines (AAAAI, AAI, ATS, SOT, ASM, ISES, ASBMB, ABRCMS, and others).
- Posters reuse manuscript figures and the through-line narrative; keep a poster template and the group's visual identity in `/assets`.
- Confirm authorship before submission; rehearse presentations as a pod.

## Dashboards and decision-support tools

Forecasting and decision tools (e.g., the RespRisk line described in the IAP) are flagship products:

- Build them reproducibly, with documented thresholds, fairness/equity checks, and clear risk tiers (e.g., green/amber/red).
- Co-develop with stakeholders; validate against real-world outcomes; report calibration, decision-curve utility, and **equity-stratified performance**.
- Version dashboards like code; never expose restricted data through a tool.

## Community briefs and bilingual communication

These close the Community-to-Clinic-to-Cloud loop:

- **Community risk briefs** translate forecasts into plain-language, actionable summaries for the communities the data come from.
- Materials are **bilingual (Spanish/English)** so they reach the people they're about.
- Briefs get PI review and respect privacy and partner relationships.
- Track real-world uptake (briefs issued, decisions supported, partner adoption) — impact is a product too.

## Quality bar for every product

Before anything leaves the group:

- It is **reproducible** (or, for non-analytic products, traceable to reproducible work).
- It **respects data governance, privacy, and DUAs.**
- Its **authorship/contributorship is documented and agreed.**
- It has been **reviewed** (peer within the pod + PI as appropriate).
- It **advances a SMART goal and the through-line** — we make products on purpose, not just to be busy.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Products are also development
Match products to mentees' growth. A first abstract, a first figure, a first reproducible notebook, a first first-authorship — each is both a research output and a rung on the development ladder (@sec-mentoring). Plan products with people's growth in mind, not just the project's needs.
:::
